stem: Simplify: $\dfrac{{=a}^{x+1}+{=a}^{x}}{{=m}\times{=a}^{x}}$. Give your answer as a whole number.
solution: Rewrite the first power with the exponent law $b^{m+n}=b^{m}\cdot b^{n}$: ${=a}^{x+1}={=a}^{x}\cdot{=a}$. The fraction becomes $\dfrac{{=a}^{x}\cdot{=a}+{=a}^{x}}{{=m}\times{=a}^{x}}$.
Take out the common factor ${=a}^{x}$ in the numerator: $\dfrac{{=a}^{x}({=a}+1)}{{=m}\times{=a}^{x}}$.
Cancel the common factor ${=a}^{x}$ from the top and the bottom: $\dfrac{{=a}+1}{{=m}}$.
notes: Basic entry point of the skill: the numerator has just two terms, the exponent is shifted by exactly 1 (the book's ex2-4-2c shifts by 3), the common factor is the single power a^x, and the arithmetic after cancelling is small. Same skeleton as the parent (split a^(x+1) with the multiplication law, take out the common factor, cancel, evaluate) and the book's own notation (\times in the denominator, answer a whole number). Parameters are built backwards so every instance is clean: pick the divisor m and the answer q, then base a = m*q - 1, so (a+1)/m = q is always a whole number >= 2 and a <= 13 (14 distinct instances; bases 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13). The variable is fixed as x. Plus sign only, so the factor is always (a + 1). Numeric answer, so no distractors and no misconception ids are attached; mc:g10m2s2-1-3:powers-outside-algebra is not targeted here. The difference-of-squares method is left to the standard and advanced tiers, where the book's questions sit (ex2-4-2i, ex2-1-34).
